subject: Request: Geo-anchoring commitment, subprocessor schedule and temporary failover plan
messages:
From: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@fintechco.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataPrivacy Team <dataprivacy@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: geo-anchoring guarantee + subprocessors schedule

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare procurement, our DPO has two parallel asks before we proceed to legal: 1) a written commitment describing how you geo-anchor customer data for EU‑resident workloads (what "anchoring" means operationally, and the limits to cross‑region processing), and 2) an up‑to-date schedule of subprocessors and whether any of them will have access to unredacted prompts or logs.

We also anticipate short planned maintenance windows where requests may briefly fail over to an alternate EU region — we need a high‑level failover plan and max window for cross‑border processing during those windows.

Can you reply with a proposed short statement we can put into our DPA addendum and attach any subprocessor list/latest schedule?

Best,
Alice
Alice Zhao
Head of Data Privacy, FinTechCo

--
Attachment: request-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: geo-anchoring guarantee + subprocessors schedule

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear asks. High level response below; I'll loop in our security and legal folks for a short addendum draft and a current subprocessor export.

1) Geo‑anchoring commitment (draft language):
Redwood will process customer workloads within the customer‑requested region (EU) by routing and placing runtime compute and persistent storage in EU Azure/GCP regions. For transient, automated failover or cache rehydration, minimal metadata and short‑lived KV cache may be routed through compatible EU zones only; cross‑border tokenization or model telemetry is not performed unless explicitly enabled by the customer. (We'll provide a one‑paragraph addendum suitable for your DPA).

2) Subprocessor schedule: We maintain a quarterly schedule; we will provide the most recent export showing all subprocessors and the classification of access (no access, metadata-only, prompt/cache access).

3) Temporary failover windows: Planned maintenance may trigger regional failover for up to 30 minutes for warm failovers and up to 4 hours for a cold recovery in rare scenarios; each event is announced with a targeted notice to admins and we'll provide SLAs/mitigations for EU‑resident workloads in your contract addendum.

I'm attaching an initial draft and will follow up with the subprocessor CSV and a more explicit DPA paragraph after legal signs off.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Sales — EMEA, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_geo-anchoring-draft_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: geo-anchoring guarantee + subprocessors schedule

Vivek —

Thanks, that draft is a good start. Legal wants clearer limits on what we mean by "minimal metadata" and explicit phrasing about log retention/access. Suggested tweaks:
- Replace "minimal metadata" with "non‑identifiable routing metadata (region, timestamp, sequence id)"
- State that unredacted prompts and customer content are stored only in the customer region and accessed only by subprocessors listed with "prompt/cache access" classification.

Also, operations prefers we avoid specific time numbers for cold recovery in public statements; suggest we offer a binding max SLA in the contract and a separate ops runbook for incident escalations.

Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: geo-anchoring guarantee + subprocessors schedule

Couple of operational notes to include in the customer‑facing paragraph:
- We do not replicate persistent customer model inputs/outputs across regions except for explicit customer opt‑in (e.g., cross‑region analytics).
- KV cache snapshotting for fast warm failovers is encrypted-at-rest and keys are regionally scoped; key escrow is handled by the customer if they choose HSM.
- Subprocessor schedule (attached) includes classification column: "none", "metadata-only", "prompt/cache access". We should send the CSV to the customer and indicate the last update date.

Attached: subprocessor_schedule_q2_2026.csv, temporary_failover_matrix.xlsx

Marissa
Head of Product — Privacy & Compliance

Alice —

Following up with the materials we discussed. Attached are: 1) a succinct one‑paragraph "Geo‑anchoring" addendum you can paste into your DPA, 2) our Q2 subprocessor schedule export (classification included), and 3) a short failover matrix summarizing planned maintenance windows and maximum binding failover SLA for EU‑resident workloads.

Quoted paragraph (for your DPA):
"Redwood will process and persist customer data for EU‑resident workloads within EU regions requested by the customer. Runtime compute, persistent storage, and audit logs for that workload will be placed in EU regions. In limited, pre‑planned or automated failover events, transient routing metadata and encrypted KV cache may be routed to another EU region; Redwood will not route unredacted customer prompts or persistent customer content outside the customer's specified region except with explicit, documented customer consent or as required by law. A list of subprocessors and their access classifications is attached and will be kept current on a quarterly cadence."
